AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which waste should NOT be put in a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bags
   B. Chicken droppings
   C. Banana peelings
   D. Fresh grass

2. Which of these is a brown material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings
   B. Fresh cow dung
   C. Fresh weeds
   D. Dry leaves

3. Why are diseased plants not added to compost? (1 mark)
   A. They make the heap too tall
   B. They are too heavy
   C. The disease can spread to the crops later
   D. They rot too slowly to count

4. Why is the water container placed on a stand? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it from birds
   B. To keep it out of the sun forever
   C. So water flows down through the pipe
   D. So it looks tall

5. Where should the holes in the pipe be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Far away from the plants
   B. Only at the end of the row
   C. Only near the bucket
   D. Next to each plant

6. Which animal is a domestic animal, not a wild one? (1 mark)
   A. Monkey
   B. Hare
   C. Squirrel
   D. Goat

7. Which part holds the head of the scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. The top of the pole
   B. The dry grass on the ground
   C. The fence
   D. The tin

8. Why should a scarecrow be moved every few days? (1 mark)
   A. It gets too hot
   B. It grows
   C. The pole is too heavy
   D. Animals get used to one that never moves

9. Which is the safest way to make holes or dig for scarecrow parts? (1 mark)
   A. Use broken glass
   B. Play with the tools
   C. Use bare hands on sharp tools
   D. Ask an adult to help

10. Why is mulch put around a young tree? (1 mark)
   A. It kills roots
   B. It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   C. It makes the tree shorter
   D. It stops flowering

11. What can an agricultural extension officer help with? (1 mark)
   A. Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   B. Building a house
   C. Selling your tools
   D. Cooking meals

12. What do flowers become in a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Trunks
   B. Roots
   C. Fruits
   D. Soil

13. What is a fruit? (1 mark)
   A. The roots of a plant
   B. The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   C. The stem of a plant
   D. The leaves of a plant

14. What is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal kept and cared for by people
   B. An animal that lives freely in the forest
   C. An animal that cannot be tamed
   D. An animal found only in parks

15. Which animal is not domestic? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Cow
   C. Elephant
   D. Hen

16. What is meant by income from animals? (1 mark)
   A. Manure used
   B. Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   C. Food eaten at home
   D. Feathers

17. Which of these is an animal welfare need? (1 mark)
   A. Being hit
   B. No shelter
   C. Clean water always available
   D. Living in mud

18. Which of these is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Goat
   C. Lion
   D. Giraffe

19. Which nutrient in milk builds strong bones and teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Sugar
   C. Calcium
   D. Starch

20. Why should hands be washed after handling chickens? (1 mark)
   A. To colour the hands
   B. To get feathers off
   C. To remove germs
   D. To warm the hands

21. Which of these is a body-building food? (1 mark)
   A. Rice
   B. Chapati
   C. Beans
   D. Cooking oil

22. Which of these gives fibre? (1 mark)
   A. Soft drinks
   B. Sweets
   C. Vegetables and fruits
   D. Sugar

23. What is shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Baking in an oven
   B. Cooking in water
   C. Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   D. Cooking in a lot of deep oil

24. Which way should you open a lid on a hot pot? (1 mark)
   A. Fast and close
   B. Away from your face
   C. Straight toward your face
   D. Under water

25. Why should the frying pan be heated before adding food? (1 mark)
   A. To burn it
   B. To melt it
   C. To break it
   D. So that food browns and does not soak up oil

26. What should you do first for a small burn? (1 mark)
   A. Put butter on it
   B. Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes
   C. Ignore it
   D. Cover with toothpaste

27. Which food is usually boiled? (1 mark)
   A. Mandazi
   B. Potatoes
   C. Chips
   D. Bhajia

28. Why should we wear shoes? (1 mark)
   A. To hide our feet
   B. To make us tall
   C. To be heavier
   D. To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers

29. Which disease can result from drinking unsafe water? (1 mark)
   A. Cholera
   B. Sunburn
   C. Toothache
   D. A cut

30. Which disease can be spread by dirty hands? (1 mark)
   A. Diarrhoea
   B. Toothache only
   C. Broken leg
   D. Sunburn

31. When should you wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Only after school ends
   B. Never
   C. Before eating and after using the toilet
   D. Only on Sunday

32. Why should you never mix cleaning chemicals? (1 mark)
   A. They will cost more
   B. They can give off harmful fumes
   C. They will look nicer
   D. They become soap

33. What is domestic hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Washing your own body
   B. Cooking meals
   C. Growing food
   D. Keeping the home and its surroundings clean

34. What is the correct order for cleaning a room? (1 mark)
   A. Dust, sweep, mop
   B. Sweep, mop, dust
   C. Mop, sweep, dust
   D. Mop, dust, sweep

35. Which method wipes dust from furniture? (1 mark)
   A. Burning
   B. Sweeping
   C. Dusting
   D. Mopping

36. Why should torn gloves not be used? (1 mark)
   A. They may not protect the hands
   B. They are too heavy
   C. They are too clean
   D. They are too big

37. Why might wet PPE stored away cause a problem? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes stronger
   B. It becomes cleaner
   C. It grows mould and smells
   D. It becomes lighter

38. What is a tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. A type of cloth
   B. A permanent decorative stitch
   C. A cutting tool
   D. A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place

39. Where should needles be kept? (1 mark)
   A. In a pin cushion or needle case
   B. In your mouth
   C. On the floor
   D. On a chair

40. What should you do at the end of a sewing lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them
   B. Hide them
   C. Count the needles and pins
   D. Throw them

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State three safety rules when using needles and scissors. (3 marks)

42. Explain why tacking thread should be loose. (2 marks)

43. Give three mistakes to avoid when sowing tiny seeds. (3 marks)

44. State three safety rules when cleaning PPE. (3 marks)

45. Write the steps for growing carrots from seed to harvest. (5 marks)

46. Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly. (4 marks)

47. State the functions of roots, leaves and flowers in a fruit tree. (3 marks)

48. How can a family get a balanced meal cheaply? (2 marks)

49. Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds. (3 marks)

50. Describe how a family can plant trees to help conserve fuel. (4 marks)

51. Name three PPE items and say what each protects. (3 marks)

52. What are tacking stitches? (2 marks)

53. Explain why a tippy tap is useful in a school without a tap. (3 marks)

54. State two ways of making drinking water safe. (2 marks)

55. Explain why vegetables and fruits should be eaten every day. (3 marks)

56. Give three reasons why nails should be kept short and clean. (3 marks)

57. What should be done with a paper dust mask that is dirty? (2 marks)

58. Explain how an improved jiko saves fuel. (3 marks)

59. Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree. (4 marks)

60. Choose PPE for gardening and say why. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Plastic bags
   Plastic does not rot and spoils the compost.

2. D — Dry leaves
   Brown materials are dry, like dry leaves, dry grass and straw.

3. C — The disease can spread to the crops later
   Disease germs may survive and infect crops when the compost is used.

4. C — So water flows down through the pipe
   A raised container gives water the push to flow down.

5. D — Next to each plant
   Water must fall near the roots.

6. D — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

7. A — The top of the pole
   The head is fixed to the top of the long pole.

8. D — Animals get used to one that never moves
   Animals learn that something still is harmless.

9. D — Ask an adult to help
   Safety comes first.

10. B — It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   Mulch reduces evaporation.

11. A — Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   Extension officers advise farmers.

12. C — Fruits
   Fruits develop from flowers.

13. B — The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds.

14. A — An animal kept and cared for by people
   Domestic animals depend on people for food, water and shelter.

15. C — Elephant
   Elephants are wild.

16. B — Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   Farmers sell products to earn money.

17. C — Clean water always available
   Animals need water, feed, shelter, health care and kind treatment.

18. B — Goat
   Goats are kept by farmers.

19. C — Calcium
   Milk has calcium and protein.

20. C — To remove germs
   Poultry can carry germs.

21. C — Beans
   Beans have protein.

22. C — Vegetables and fruits
   Fibre helps digestion.

23. C — Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer of oil.

24. B — Away from your face
   Steam can burn.

25. D — So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   Food placed in cold oil soaks up oil.

26. B — Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes
   Cooling reduces burn damage.

27. B — Potatoes
   Potatoes are commonly boiled.

28. D — To protect feet from injury, worms and jiggers
   Shoes protect the feet.

29. A — Cholera
   Cholera spreads through dirty water.

30. A — Diarrhoea
   Germs on hands can get into the mouth.

31. C — Before eating and after using the toilet
   These are key times.

32. B — They can give off harmful fumes
   Mixing chemicals is dangerous.

33. D — Keeping the home and its surroundings clean
   It is care of the home environment.

34. A — Dust, sweep, mop
   Dust falls, so dust before sweeping.

35. C — Dusting
   Dusting removes dust from surfaces.

36. A — They may not protect the hands
   Holes let dirt and germs in.

37. C — It grows mould and smells
   Moulds grow in damp places.

38. D — A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place
   Tacking is removed later.

39. A — In a pin cushion or needle case
   Needles are sharp.

40. C — Count the needles and pins
   Counting ensures none is lost.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never put needles in the mouth; keep them in a pin cushion; count them; carry scissors with points down (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tight thread pulls and wrinkles the cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pulls, 1 mark for wrinkles.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leaving big lumps in the seedbed, sowing too deep, sowing too thick without thinning, or watering strongly (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use soap and clean water; keep buckets and brushes from small children; wash your hands after; clean in an open place with drainage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare a fine seedbed; make drills about 1 cm deep; sow seeds thinly with sand; cover and water gently; thin to about 5 cm; weed and water; harvest after three to four months by loosening the soil and pulling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the tree and take in water; leaves make food using sunlight; flowers form fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Grow vegetables and fruits at home and use cheap proteins such as beans, omena or eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each crop.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant fast growing trees on their land for firewood, care for them and replace any tree cut with more new trees, so wood is always available and forests are not cut.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for planting, caring, replacing and result.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Large, loose temporary stitches used to hold cloth in place before permanent sewing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for temporary, 1 mark for holding cloth.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: It saves water, it can be made cheaply from a container, and children do not touch the container with dirty hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Boil and cool it covered; use a filter or treatment tablets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals, fibre for digestion and water, so they protect the body from disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs hide under nails, worm eggs are found there, and long nails can scratch and cause injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is thrown away and replaced, not washed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for throwing, 1 mark for replacing.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Its walls keep the heat close to the pot, so food cooks faster, and less charcoal or wood is used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat close to pot, 1 mark for faster cooking, 1 mark for less fuel.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands from dirt and cuts; gumboots protect feet from mud; hat protects the head from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with reason.
